messages:
tom: Hey all  heads up: partner due 2025-03-02, I'm planning ~12 weeks parental leave. Quick Qs: when to start paperwork, can I split the leave into two chunks, and what happens to pay & benefits? cc @jen (People Ops)

jen (People Ops): Congrats Tom! 389 Best practice: start ~30 days before. Splits are allowed (usually up to 2 blocks in first 12 months) but need manager + People Ops approval so we can calculate top-ups and benefits windows.

sam (Payroll): Payroll note: Redwood provides an 8-week company top-up for eligible FT staff. If you have STD, that offsets company pay; you should file STD as soon as leave starts to avoid delays. We need approved leave docs before the pay period close (about 7 days before payout) to make the top-up on time. Retro pay is possible but slower.

lisa (Benefits): Health coverage: employer share continues for up to 12 weeks of approved leave. If unpaid beyond that, you'll either pay employee share or elect COBRA. I'll DM the estimate and the benefits-continuation form.

nina (Manager): Coverage plan: I can reassign on-call to Kate and pause a few low-priority projects. Tom, can you create a 10-day handoff doc + a 2-week overlap plan? I'll book overlap time.

kate: Happy to cover on-call and the weekly sync. If you add a short runbook for common alerts that'd help a lot.

jen (People Ops): Quick checklist: - Fill internal leave request: https://redwoodinference.hq/leave-request - Upload birth/placement docs - File STD claim if applicable - Manager sign-off on coverage + return plan - People Ops confirms benefit continuation dates - Payroll sync meeting before first payroll cutoff

hr-bot: Reminder: 'Start parental leave paperwork' scheduled 3 weeks before 2025-03-02 on your calendar, tom.

tom: Thanks everyone 60a I'll submit the form today and draft the handoff doc. Appreciate the help!
__notes: Single-thread Slack document; messages in chronological order; no title field per agents.md
